topic: The Hidden Symmetry: From Ternary Counting to Sierpinski Fractals
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

outline.topic: The Hidden Symmetry: From Ternary Counting to Sierpinski Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: The Bridge: From Binary to Ternary Counting
sections.content: Introduce the base-3 system (0, 1, 2) as a representational tool for branching decisions. Explain that each digit corresponds to a 'choice' in a 3-way path, creating a foundation for recursive structures.
sections.example: A smart robot moving through a 3-way branching tunnel; each digit in a ternary number (e.g., 012) dictates its turn at each junction.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the variation of Towers of Hanoi where disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Connect this to the ternary system: every move state corresponds to a unique ternary string.
sections.example: Representing the 3-peg system as a state-space graph where nodes are configurations and edges are legal moves. A 3-disk game results in 3^3 = 27 possible states.

sections.title: Visualizing the State Space: The Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Demonstrate that the state-space graph of the constrained Towers of Hanoi, when projected onto a 2D plane, forms the vertices of a Sierpinski Triangle. Explain self-similarity: the structure of 1 disk is a miniature of the structure of n disks.
sections.example: An animation morphing a standard graph of move-states into a growing triangle, showing how the 'path' of the optimal solution traces the edges of the fractal.

sections.title: Synthesis: Decoding the Fractal
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts by showing how a ternary string acts as an address for a specific position within the Sierpinski Triangle. This demonstrates that recursion is not just code, but spatial geometry.
sections.example: A 'fractal hiker' using a ternary map to navigate precisely to the center of a nested triangle, illustrating the isomorphism between counting systems and geometric fractals.

storyboard.title: The Bridge: From Binary to Ternary Counting
lecture_lines: Base-3 digits represent distinct three-way branch choices.
Each digit dictates one specific path at every junction.
Ternary counting naturally generates recursive, branching structures.

storyboard.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Disks move only between adjacent pegs in this variation.
Each move state maps uniquely to a ternary string.
Three disks create twenty-seven possible state configurations.
animations: Display three peg setup in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate moving disk from peg A to B using arc path.
Highlight illegal move restriction in red (#FF6347).

storyboard.title: Visualizing the State Space: The Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Projecting move-states reveals the Sierpinski Triangle structure.
Small disk structures nest within larger recursive patterns.
The optimal solution path traces the fractal edges.

Add three smaller triangles iteratively in blue (#00BFFF).
Fill the Sierpinski pattern showing depth 3 in light grey (#D3D3D3).

storyboard.title: Synthesis: Decoding the Fractal
lecture_lines: Ternary strings serve as addresses in the fractal geometry.
Recursive counting perfectly maps to nested spatial structures.
Geometry emerges directly from the structure of recursive logic.

Overlay binary counting sequence onto triangle nodes in yellow (#FFFFE0).
Highlight total moves formula as N=3^k in light cyan (#E0FFFF).
